notes: SHAPE CHOSEN: shape 1, the DEFER-to-load-complete variant, and it reuses the seam the repo already has. Shape 2 (make the assertion patient) was rejected on evidence, not taste: syncFromModel early-returns unless model.revision > ctx.lastApplied (SyncFromModelSystem.ts:398), so setHudDisplay is NOT called per frame. Whether a glyph appears therefore depends on how many board-stats events have happened, not on whether the glyph resolves; a patient assertion makes the gate green while the spectator canvas still shows no glyph, which is the same 'delete the assertion' failure the audit exists to stop, in a new position.

The deferral seam already exists one function away: ensureIcon (SyncFromModelSystem.ts:68-94) returns a placeholder key and hooks scene.load.once(Phaser.Loader.Events.COMPLETE) into st._iconCb, which the scene wires as SyncContext.onIconsReady -> refreshOccupantIcons (LawnWorldScene.ts:249-252). Band B was never wired into it. So the fix EXTENDS the one existing art-ready refresh rather than adding a second loader path - which is what makes it the SOLID answer and the awaitable variant wrong here: syncFromModel is a synchronous function, so an awaitable loader would have no caller able to await it.

A naive deferral would INTRODUCE an infinite 404 retry loop, because the current condition re-issues scene.load.image whenever the key is absent and the loader is idle - and after a FILE_LOAD_ERROR the key is still absent. The fix therefore reuses the existing _iconFails memo (SyncFromModelSystem.ts:100-110, noteIconLoadFailure in lawnSyncGate.ts:24-32) instead of adding a second failure record. That memo is keyed by texture key, so it covers the actor-hud-element-* keys with no change to the error handler.

LAYOUT, measured by reading rather than assumed: the identity row's initial centring is computed from `widths`, which reserves element space from the CATALOG presentation (primarySize/secondarySize), not from texture availability (ActorHudDisplay.ts:101-109). The early return at :133 therefore leaves a correctly-sized hole that is already centred, and the element loop is last in the row so nothing after it reads identityX. Filling that hole later on load-complete cannot move the row, so the fix carries no relayout regression - which is itself asserted by a test.

MECHANISM MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, AND IT OVERTURNED MY OWN THEORY. On the reverted rebuilt bundle a probe counted Band B draws across 20 polls / ~6.5s / four board-stats poll cycles: draws=1, glyph=false throughout, epochs=0. So the audit's benign 'false,false,true,true' is only the BUSY-board form; on a quiet board the glyph NEVER appears. And epochs=0 DISPROVES the masking theory I had formed while reading the code - I believed lawn:iconEpoch was force-resyncing the scene (LawnWorldScene.ts:221-227 sets lastApplied=0) and hiding the race. It fired zero times. LawnPage.tsx:181 does poll board-stats every 1500ms, but every poll 404s in the mocked environment so it never bumps the revision and never redraws; it is not what saved the pre-fix build either.

MEASUREMENT WINDOW, chosen so it cannot read an absence as a presence. Every one of the five events carries `elements` BY CONSTRUCTION, because the recorded caution is that a real Peashooter's first two HUD events carried elements=null and a window starting at board entry would be a third false red. A first attempt sent the same fire/ice element five times and reported firstSample=true from event 2 onward - which proves only that the texture was CACHED, not that event 2 survived a race. The published run uses FIVE DISTINCT ELEMENTS (fire, ice, air, earth, light) so each event's texture has never been requested and each is a genuine first-load race. The naive run is not reported as a result; it is the reason the window is shaped this way.

FIVE-EVENT RAW SEQUENCE, fixed build: event1 fire firstSample=false -> glyphWithin5s=true; event2 ice false->true; event3 air false->true; event4 earth false->true; event5 light false->true (3.6s). Same measurement, fix reverted and rebuilt: false -> glyphWithin5s=false for all five (28.7s, each burning the full 5s budget). Five false->true against five false->false, over five distinct events and five distinct textures.

TWO DEFECTS FOUND IN MY OWN CHANGE AND FIXED BEFORE COMMIT, both by asking what the change implied rather than what it did. (1) A naive deferral LOOPS FOREVER on a 404, because the pre-fix condition re-issues scene.load.image whenever the key is absent and the loader is idle, and a key is still absent after FILE_LOAD_ERROR. Fixed by reusing the existing _iconFails memo, which is keyed by texture key and so covers actor-hud-element-* with no change to the existing error handler. (2) bustLawnIconTextures cleared the shared memos WHOLESALE; once glyphs share them, an icon epoch landing mid-glyph-load would forget an in-flight request and the next repaint would re-request a key the loader is already fetching. A type icon's key embeds the epoch and is genuinely stale; a glyph's carries no epoch. The bust is now scoped to icon-, with a test.
